messages:
Maya: heads-up — saw a reproducible p95 latency regression (~18-25%) on long-seq runs when the runtime picks the paged FlashAttention path together with fused RoPE/ALiBi.
Jonathan: which model/config and exact kernel path? any recent commits that touch selector?
Maya: model=redwood/13b-like, seq=8192, batch=1, quant=q4_0. Kernel selector root changed by PR #3462 last night (kernel priority and rotary handling). Repro command I used:
```
./perf/bench --model redwood/13b-like --seq_len 8192 --batch 1 --kernel auto --threads 1 --warmups 5 --iters 30
```
Outputs: p95 went from 220ms -> 270ms on A6000.
perf-bot: perf run: https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/1934567890 (artifacts attached)
Samir: I repro locally. Quick perf trace shows a memcpy spike right before attention kernel dispatch. Looks like when fused-rope is enabled we take the paged_flash_v2 path which expects different Q/K packing. Flame snippet:
```
0.12s memcpy (kv_page_fetch)
0.09s pack_qk (layout_xform)
0.25s paged_flash_v2
```
That pack_qk step didn't exist on the non-paged flash path.
Olivia: sounds like the kernel_selector is not considering rotary_scaling/rotary_dim remap compat. If rotary_scale != 1.0 or rotary_dim != head_dim it may require an extra transpose to match paged kernel layout.
Ara: we added a heuristic in #3452 that prefers paged_flash for seq>4096 and estimated_tokens>1e6. Maybe it assumed packing parity with fused-rope. Could be regressed by #3462.
Jonathan: any regression delta on memory footprint? does KV page cache behavior change eviction frequency?
Maya: memory stays ~same, but KV page fetches increase ~15% due to slightly larger page prefetch/window when using paged kernel (we saw extra page touches). That triggers more memcpy as Samir saw.
Samir: I bisected quickly: commit range 3456..3462 shows the switch. Specifically commit 3460 changed ordering in kernel_selector: it moved paged_flash above fused_attention_smallq for auto mode.
Olivia: mitigation ideas: (a) add a compatibility check in selector that ensures packed_layout == kernel.expected_layout for fused-rope/rotary_scale combos; (b) prefer fallback flash path when rotary_scale != 1.0 until we implement an in-kernel remap; (c) tweak page prefetch window to avoid extra memcpy.
Ara: also add a lightweight probe in tracing to record kernel_layout and rotary_flags per request. That'll help quantify how often selector chooses incompatible pair.
Maya: proposed plan:
1) revert ordering change in selector for auto mode (hotfix) -> quick perf run.
2) add compatibility predicate for rotary_scale/rotary_dim and unit test coverage.
3) instrument KV page eviction and memcpy counters in tracing.
I can take 1+2, Samir can do 3.
Samir: will add counters and a small microbench to exercise pack_qk path. Also will reproduce with different rotary_scale values (0.99,1.0,1.01) to see sensitivity.
Jonathan: sgtm. @perf-bot can you spawn 3 bench runs with tags: "hotfix-selector-revert", "rotary-probe", "page-counter" and mark priority high?
perf-bot: queued perf jobs: https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/1934567901 , https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/1934567902 , https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/1934567903
Status: queued
Maya: thanks. I'll open a PR with revert + predicate and link here once ready.
Olivia: if revert shows improvement we should plan the longer-term work (in-kernel remap or unify layouts).
Ara: logging: add a TODO to product-tracking for long-seq SLO risk if selector oscillates.
Maya: noted. will update once perf jobs finish.
